title: Choose the visual world for RadarPro
question: The roll assigned Night Road Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Night Road Atlas
options.lineage: Rand McNally road atlas read by dome light
options.thesis: The chaser's oldest companion, the road atlas, reprinted for night: the map owns the page and index tabs run its edges.
options.viewport: Full-bleed dark map with a margin grid (A-H across, 1-9 down); product thumb tabs on the right edge, tilts as mile markers beneath; a slim top line with site and scan time; the bottom time strip runs observed scans into forecast beyond NOW.
options.risk: Atlas red and blue sit near radar palette colours; they must stay in the chrome and never touch the data.

raised.raise: Neutrals snap to one stepped ramp of 9 tones; no ad-hoc greys.
One region owns the frame: the map runs edge to edge, chrome lives only on its margins.
The site picker is a dense ICAO code grid keyed to the dots on the map.
No boxes or button chrome: labels are the controls, and selection fills them.
The margin grid is a real layer: probe readouts cite their cell (C4), and it can be toggled.

options.label: Interstate Guide Sign
options.lineage: MUTCD overhead guide signs and route shields
options.thesis: What chasers read through the windshield for hours: retroreflective white on sign green, built to be read at 70 mph.
options.viewport: An overhead sign gantry across the top centre names site and product, with an exit tab for the tilt; shields switch sites; the rest is map.
options.risk: Sign green sits on top of reflectivity greens, and road signs are the obvious read of 'chasing'.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.thesis: The radar is the terrain and never edits; everything the chaser marks rides above it in one purple.
options.viewport: Map full-bleed; probe points, cross-section line and chosen site drawn as purple controls; a control-description table on the left lists them.
options.case: Holds product clarity (data and annotation can never be confused) but chasers don't recognise orienteering.
options.risk: Purple overlays collide with the magenta of high reflectivity and hail.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step zone ramp.
options.case: Chasers don't recognise it, and hatching over echoes hurts clarity.
options.kept: One stepped tonal ramp as the only neutrals.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Flat colour lobes divided by coastline.
options.case: Toy-like for severe weather; a light ground breaks the dark constraint.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Stamp-sized cells keyed to a hall map.
options.case: No recognition; the newsprint ground breaks the dark constraint.
options.kept: Dense code grid keyed to map positions.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type as the interface.
options.risk: Light-weight type is unreadable in a moving vehicle.
options.case: Panorama panes would cover the map, and it reads as another OS.
options.kept: Chrome deleted; type is the control.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid as the design.
options.kept: The grid as a real, toggleable state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: RadarScope / GR2Analyst-style workstation, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Top toolbar with product and tilt buttons, a layers list on the left, map in the rest, a time slider at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
